findings: v3: real Gemini prints replace the stand-in for entries; see "Evidence: real Gemini signals". The rows below are the earlier stand-in test.
Losses stay small: the average losing trade was −9% to −11%, against −55% to −64% drawdowns for buy-and-hold.
Win rate is 33–46%. The edge comes from winners 3–9× the size of losers, not from winning most trades.
Crypto reverses fast, so most of a crypto position should leave on the daily flip; stocks trend longer, so most should ride the weekly.
The BTC weekly trend filter helped crypto (+54% vs +43%, drawdown −26% vs −31%). The S&P 200-day filter did almost nothing for stocks, so it only trims size.
The rules lag in strong bulls: they kept 28–48% of bull-quarter gains. That is the price of the small losses.
Robust, not tuned to a peak: 10 of 12 nearby settings were positive for crypto and 12 of 12 for stocks. The 14/2 setting sits mid-plateau.
Both halves of the window held up: crypto +38% (2021–24) and +43% (2024–26) vs buy-and-hold −30% and +402% (ZEC-driven); stocks +32% and +174% vs +23% and +299%.
untested: Business, TAM and crowd-cycle pillars: judgment, not backtested.
Fear & Greed and funding gauges: read for regime context only.
Euphoria trim (weekly RSI over 85): small drawdown gain, small return cost; kept optional.
Banking a third at +1R raised win rate to 46% (crypto) and 55% (stocks) but cut crypto returns from +54% to +7%; not adopted.
Universe picked today, so stock results carry survivorship bias; the crypto window starts at the 2021 top.

gemini.source: Real Gemini Accumulator labels (Buy, Max Buy, Trim) read off the TradingView Opulence chart history on Nov 15, 2026: each label found by its colour and text on a screenshot, dated with the chart's own time scale. Weekly: 39 names (13 crypto, 26 stocks), 177 Buys and 49 Max Buys since Nov 2021. Daily: 18 names (13 crypto, 5 stocks: NVDA, TSLA, ALAB, HOOD, AVGO), 603 Buys and 50 Max Buys; the other daily names were not read because the TradingView session ended mid-scan.
gemini.real: Real: every entry signal (chart prints). Stand-in: the Money Line used for confirmation and exits is still the Supertrend(14, 2) copy. Checks: 4 names read twice gave identical lists; 5 of 5 weekly prints the desk logged live in October (NVDA, ALAB, ASML, AMZN Buy Oct 19; LEU Max Buy Oct 12) sit on the same bar in history. 2 September desk prints (LEU weekly Max Buy, POWL weekly Buy, Sep 22–24) are not in history, so a print counts only after the weekly close.

findings: Stocks: the weekly Max Buy is the real edge. Waiting for the weekly Money Line to turn up after it won 85% of 13 trades (88% and 80% in the two halves). Without waiting it won 78% of 23 but the losers were bigger (−26%).
Stocks: a plain weekly Buy is weaker (54–58% win) but 82% of them were higher a year later when the weekly Money Line confirmed.

Crypto: the claim does not hold in this window. Weekly Max Buys won 50–59%; the May–June 2022 Max Buys failed into the bear market. 2024–26 alone: 67–75%. Requiring BTC's weekly uptrend made it worse (Max Buys print at bottoms).
Daily signals are weaker than weekly on both: daily Buys win 38–47%. The daily Max Buy on stocks (71%) has only 7 trades.
Signal-bar-low stops wrecked the results (9–33% win): Gemini buys into weakness, so the stop has to sit on a weekly close below the signal bar's low minus one weekly ATR.
The trade-off: these rules sit in cash most of the time, so basket totals trail buy-and-hold in a bull run (stocks +31% to +70% vs +388%). The low drawdown is partly low exposure.
caveats: Labels on history may differ from what printed live (repaint); October live prints matched, two September ones did not.
Small samples for Max Buy: 13–24 stock trades, 9–22 crypto. Treat the 85% as "strong", not exact.
Pixel reading can miss labels that overlap at the 4-pixel weekly zoom; a second zoomed pass covered 2023–26.
